newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX starts sharply down on Wall St tumble.
newsitem.headline: German DAX starts sharply down on Wall St tumble.

text.p: German shares tracked Wall Street to an early tumble on Friday, as a 100-point drop on the Dow Jones index revived memories of last Friday's market rout.
The blue chip DAX index was down 40.71 points, or 1.4 percent, at 2,806.37 points after a half hour of trade and some dealers were concerned that worse was to come.
"After all, it's Friday the 13th," said one Frankfurt dealer. "I am sure there are more people out there who will come in later and sell."
Indications from the futures market, where December DAX futures were down 47.5 points at 2,802.5, pointed to a greater downside risk, dealers said.
A early technical failure at the Frankfurt stock exchange which had wiped out pre-bourse electronic stock dealing for more than an hour contributed to the market's uncertainty.
But the main pressure came after the Dow Jones Index lost 1.5 percent on Thursday amid a late wave of computer-driven selling -- its biggest loss since mid-July.
"Fundamentally, there is no real justification for the German market to be under this kind of pressure," another dealer said. "But we just can't get away from Wall Street."

There was little attention on corporate news and Volkswagen AG was more stable than the market average even as public prosecutors detailed the criminal charges against its former management board member, Jose Ignacio Lopez de Arriortua.
